Customer: Okay, okay, I trust you. Just send the payment link for the 20,000 rupees. I will do it right now before I forget.

Customer: Got it. I'm opening it now... yes, I see it. Doing the payment... okay, done! I got the confirmation. Reference number is UPI/2024/891456.

Agent: Excellent, Rajesh! Thank you for that. I can see the payment has been received. Your new outstanding balance is now 27,500 rupees. Now, for the remaining amount — you mentioned the 28th or 29th. Can you commit to the 29th so we have a clear date?

Customer: Yes, yes, 29th is fine. My salary always comes by the 28th, so by 29th I will definitely have it.

Customer: Yes, I have it. Don't worry, I will pay on time. I don't want any more calls after this.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. We appreciate your cooperation. Just to recap — 20,000 rupees paid today, and 27,500 rupees by the 29th. We'll follow up on the 29th. Thank you for your time.

Customer: Yeah, okay. What is it about? I've been meaning to call you people actually.

Agent: Great, so I'm calling about your outstanding balance of 47,300 rupees which was due on the 15th of this month. We haven't received payment yet. Can you help me understand what's happening?

Customer: No no, I know, I know. I actually tried to pay yesterday. I attempted the payment through the UPI app — you know, the Google Pay app — and it just... it kept saying transaction failed. I tried three times, Priya. Three times the payment didn't go through.

Agent: Oh, I see. So you do have the funds available?

Customer: Yes, yes, absolutely. The money is there in my account. I checked the balance and everything. It's just that the app is not working properly. Every time I try to send the money to your payment link, it says "Transaction Declined" and then the amount gets blocked for like 24 hours. It's very frustrating.

Agent: I completely understand, Rajesh. This is actually quite common — sometimes there are gateway issues on our end or the UPI infrastructure itself has a glitch. Let me help you with this. Have you tried using a different payment method?

Customer: No, I haven't. I don't really know what else to do. I mean, I have net banking access with my ICICI account. Can I transfer the money directly through that?

Agent: Absolutely, that's a perfect option. You can do an NEFT or IMPS transfer directly to our account. Let me give you the details. Our account number is 0012457896543, IFSC code is FINS0000123. The account is under Finserve Loans Limited.

Customer: Okay, okay, let me write this down. 0012457896543, and the IFSC is FINS0000123. Got it. And the account name?

Agent: Finserve Loans Limited. You can do this transfer right now if you'd like, or whenever you're ready. IMPS will be instant, so the payment should reflect in our system within minutes.

Customer: Actually, I can do it right now. I'm at home and my laptop is right here. But Priya, one thing — I want to make sure this goes through because I've had issues with net banking before too. How long will it take to show up in your system?

Agent: If you use IMPS, it should be instant — within 5 to 10 minutes maximum. If you use NEFT, it might take a couple of hours depending on the bank's processing time. I'd recommend IMPS for speed.

Customer: Okay, IMPS it is. Let me just... let me log into my net banking now. Alright, I'm in. I'm entering your account details now. 0012457896543, right?

Agent: Yes, that's correct. And the amount is 47,300 rupees.

Customer: Okay, I've entered everything. Now it's asking me to confirm. Alright, I'm clicking submit. Oh wait, it's processing... Yes! It says "Transaction Successful". The reference number is IMPS2024112847563. Did you get that?

Agent: That's wonderful, Rajesh! Let me note that down — IMPS2024112847563. The payment should reflect in our system very shortly. Can you give me that reference number one more time just to be sure?

Customer: IMPS2024112847563. Yes.

Agent: Perfect. Thank you so much for being proactive about this and for trying multiple times yesterday. I really appreciate your cooperation. The payment should show up in our records within the next 10 minutes or so. Once it's confirmed, your account will be updated and you won't see any further collection calls.

Customer: Great, thank you. I'm glad we could sort this out. I was worried because the UPI thing wasn't working and I didn't know what to do.

Agent: I completely understand. These technical issues can be stressful. Just to confirm — if for any reason this IMPS transfer doesn't go through, which is unlikely, you have my reference number here and you can reach out to us again, okay? But I'm confident this will process smoothly.

Customer: Okay, sounds good. Thanks again, Priya.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Vikram Desai?

Customer: Yes, speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Vikram, this is Ananya from Finserve Collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 7834. Do you have a couple of minutes?

Customer: Haan, yes, I know about it. What's the issue? I've been meaning to sort this out actually.

Agent: Great, thanks for taking my call. So I'm looking at your account here — you're currently overdue by 38 days. The outstanding balance is Rs. 87,650. Can we talk about getting this resolved?

Customer: Yes, yes, I want to pay, Ananya. I really do. But right now I'm having a problem with my bank account. It's on hold.

Agent: On hold? Can you tell me what happened?

Customer: Two weeks back, HDFC called me and said my account is frozen. They mentioned something about KYC compliance review — they said my documents need to be re-verified or something. I've been with them for almost five years, never had any issue before. Now suddenly this.

Agent: I see. So your account is frozen due to a KYC compliance review by HDFC. That means you can't withdraw or transfer anything from that account right now, is that correct?

Customer: Exactly. I have the money sitting there, but I cannot touch it. I tried to use my debit card yesterday and it was declined. I cannot do any transfers, no withdrawals, nothing. It's very frustrating.

Agent: I completely understand. This is a bank-side issue, not something we can resolve directly. Have you contacted HDFC to find out what documents they need or when this will be resolved?

Customer: I called them twice already. They keep saying the same thing — "Your account is under review, please wait." When I asked how long, they said maybe one week, maybe ten days. They're not giving me a clear timeline.

Agent: Okay, so potentially one to two weeks. In the meantime, do you have access to any other account? A joint account, another bank, or maybe a family member's account you could use?

Customer: <interruption> No, I don't have another account. My mother has an account with ICICI, but she's not comfortable using it for my loan payment. She said no, it's her personal account.

Agent: What about other payment methods — UPI, cheque, or could you deposit cash at our branch?

Customer: UPI is linked to my HDFC account, so that won't work. I don't have a cheque book right now. And going to the branch... Ananya, I'm working from home these days and the branch is quite far. I don't have time during working hours.

Agent: I understand. Let me document this properly. So your primary account is frozen due to a KYC compliance review by HDFC, expected to be resolved within one to two weeks. You don't have immediate access to alternate payment channels. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, that's correct. But I want to be very clear — I'm not refusing to pay. I have the money. It's just stuck in the account right now. I will pay as soon as the hold is lifted. I promise you.

Agent: I absolutely believe you, Vikram. This is an operational issue, not a willingness issue. When you say one to two weeks, can you give me a specific date when you expect the hold to be lifted?

Customer: The bank said maybe by next Wednesday, but they weren't very sure. I'd say by the 12th of next month at the latest. That's what they mentioned.

Agent: Perfect. So we can schedule a follow-up call for the 13th of next month. By then your account should be unfrozen. Once the hold is lifted, how quickly can you make the payment?

Customer: Within one or two days, I can transfer the full amount. I've been saving for this. I just need my account to be unfrozen.

Agent: Excellent. I'm going to log this as an operational blockage due to a bank-imposed account hold for KYC compliance review. I'll schedule a follow-up callback for the 13th of next month. At that time, we can arrange the payment immediately. If the hold is lifted earlier, please call us back on 1800-FINSERVE, that's 1800-346-7738. You can call between 9 AM and 7 PM, Monday to Friday. Just mention your account number 7834 and your name. Is there anything else I should know?

Customer: No, I think that covers it. Thank you for understanding. I was worried you'd think I was trying to avoid paying.

Agent: Not at all, Vikram. We understand that sometimes there are circumstances beyond your control. You've been very transparent with me, and I appreciate that. We'll speak again on the 13th. Take care.

Customer: Thank you, Ananya. Goodbye.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya calling from Finserve Collections. I'm reaching out regarding your personal loan account with us. Do you have a few minutes to speak?

Customer: Haan, okay, but I'm a bit busy right now. What is this about?

Agent: I'm calling about your loan account ending in 4782. Your account is currently overdue by about three months now, and the outstanding balance is showing as 2,47,500 rupees. We haven't received any payment since June. Can you help me understand what's happening?

Customer: <interruption> Two forty-seven thousand? That doesn't sound right to me. I think the amount is much less than that. When I last checked, it was around 1,80,000 or so. There's something wrong with your calculation, no?

Agent: I understand your concern, Rajesh. Let me explain — the outstanding principal was around 1,80,000, but we've added the interest that has accrued over these three months, plus a late payment penalty of 5,000 rupees. That's how we arrived at 2,47,500. But I can definitely send you a detailed breakup if you'd like to see exactly where each rupee is going.

Customer: Haan, that would be good. I want to see the breakup. Because honestly, I'm not sure about all these charges. The interest seems very high, and I don't even know if this penalty is correct. <pause> But listen, I'm not saying I won't pay. I just want to understand what I'm actually paying for, you know?

Agent: Absolutely, that's very fair. I'll email you a detailed statement within the next hour showing the principal, interest month-by-month, and the penalty charges separately. Once you review it, we can discuss the best way forward. Are you open to exploring a settlement option if the amount is confirmed?

Customer: Settlement? What do you mean by settlement? Like, paying less than what's owed?

Agent: Yes, exactly. Since your account is now in the NPA category — that's non-performing asset — the bank does have some flexibility to offer a reduced settlement amount if you can pay a lump sum or structured payments. It's not guaranteed, but it's something we can explore once you've reviewed the statement and confirmed the amount you believe you owe.

Customer: <interruption> Okay, okay, I see. So you're saying if I can pay some amount now, maybe you can reduce the total? How much reduction are we talking about? Like, 10 percent, 20 percent?

Agent: That depends on several factors — your payment capacity, how quickly you can settle, and the bank's assessment of your case. But typically, settlements in your range could see anywhere from 15 to 30 percent reduction. I can't promise a specific number right now, but once I have your confirmation on the outstanding amount and your ability to pay, I can escalate this to my manager for a formal settlement offer.

Customer: Hmm, that sounds interesting. But I need to see the breakup first. And honestly, I'm also not sure if I can pay the full amount even with a discount right now. My business has been slow for the last few months. Can you send me the settlement calculation as well? Like, what would be the settlement amount if I pay now versus if I pay in installments?

Agent: <interruption> Of course, Rajesh. That's a very practical question. Once you confirm the outstanding amount after reviewing the statement, I can prepare two scenarios for you — one for a lump sum settlement and one for a structured settlement over, say, three to six months. Both will show you the reduced amount you'd need to pay. Does that work?

Customer: Yes, yes, that works. But I want everything in writing, okay? I don't want to commit to anything over the phone and then find out later that the numbers are different. Can you send me a formal settlement offer letter?

Agent: Absolutely. I'll send you the detailed statement first, then once you confirm the amount, I'll prepare a formal settlement offer letter with both scenarios — lump sum and installment-based. You can review it, discuss with your family if needed, and then get back to me. How many days do you need to review everything?

Customer: Give me about five to seven days. I need to check my cash flow, talk to my accountant, and see what I can manage. After that, I'll call you back or you can call me. But please send the documents by tomorrow, okay?

Agent: Perfect, Rajesh. I'll send the statement and settlement scenarios by tomorrow morning. You review at your pace, and we'll connect again in five to seven days. In the meantime, if you have any questions about the breakup, just call me back. Is this the best number to reach you?

Customer: Yes, this number is fine. But please don't call me too many times before I've had a chance to review, okay? I'll get back to you once I've looked at everything.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. I won't call you until you reach out or after seven days, whichever comes first. Thank you for your time, and I look forward to resolving this with you soon.

Customer: Okay, thanks. Bye.

Customer: Ah yes, yes, I know about this. Actually, the thing is, that day my account was... there was some issue with the bank. I had the money, but the ECS bounce happened because of their system problem, not because I didn't have funds.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. These things do happen sometimes. So you're saying you had sufficient balance on the 15th when the ECS was presented?

Customer: Exactly, exactly. I had the money sitting there. But you know how it is — the bank's system was down or something. I called them and they said it was a technical issue on their end. So now I have this bounce fee added on top, which is frustrating because it's not my fault.

Agent: I completely understand your frustration. Let me check your account... yes, I can see the bounce fee of 500 rupees has been applied. So the total outstanding now is 13,000 rupees — the original EMI plus the bounce fee. Now, the good news is that we can re-present the ECS. Since you confirm you have the funds available, we can schedule a fresh ECS presentation for a date that works for you. When would be a good time?

Customer: <interruption> Wait, wait — before we do that, I want to make sure this bounce fee is actually justified. I mean, I had the money. It was the bank's fault. Why should I pay 500 rupees for something that wasn't my mistake?

Agent: That's a fair question, Rajesh. The bounce fee is standard across the industry when an ECS fails, regardless of the reason — it's charged by the lender as a processing cost for the failed transaction and the re-presentation effort. However, I can note your dispute about the bounce fee in your account, and you can raise it formally with our grievance team if you'd like. But for now, if we re-present the ECS, you would be paying the full 13,000 rupees including the fee. Does that work for you?

Customer: Hmm, okay, okay. I don't like it, but I understand. So if I agree to this re-presentation, when would you try to collect again?

Agent: Good question. We typically schedule the re-presentation for 5 to 7 days after the original failed date. Since your ECS failed on the 15th, I can schedule the re-presentation for the 22nd of this month. That gives you a week to ensure your account has sufficient balance. Does the 22nd work for you?

Customer: The 22nd... yes, that should be fine. My salary usually comes in around the 20th, so by the 22nd I'll definitely have the money. But I want to confirm — you're going to use the same ECS mandate that was already registered, right? I don't have to sign anything new?

Customer: Yes, yes, I can confirm. By the 22nd, after my salary comes, I'll have more than enough. So we're all set then? The ECS will be re-presented on the 22nd for the full 13,000?

Agent: Perfect, Rajesh. Let me just confirm the details with you. We are re-presenting the ECS on the 22nd of this month for a total of 13,000 rupees, which includes your original EMI of 12,500 and the bounce fee of 500. You've confirmed that you'll maintain sufficient balance in your account for this re-presentation. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, that's correct. And if this goes through on the 22nd, my account will be back to normal, right? No more calls about this?

Agent: Correct. Once the re-presentation is successful on the 22nd, your account will be current and you won't hear from us regarding this overdue amount. However, please remember that your next regular EMI will still be due on the 5th of next month, so you'll need to ensure that's paid on time as well.

Customer: Understood. Thank you for explaining all this. I appreciate it.

Agent: You're welcome, Rajesh. We've scheduled the re-presentation for the 22nd. You should receive an SMS confirmation shortly. If you have any questions before then, feel free to reach out. Thank you for your time, and we look forward to receiving your payment on the 22nd.

Customer: No, I don't. I mean, I have maybe 3,000 rupees I could scrape together, but that's it. And I need that for food and utilities. I'm not refusing to pay, but I genuinely cannot afford the full amount right now.

Agent: I understand. Let me ask you a few more questions so I can help you properly. What was your monthly salary before the job loss?

Customer: Around 45,000 rupees. It was a decent salary for my family. But now, nothing is coming in.

Customer: Yes, 18,500. I have been paying it regularly for three years, but now I cannot. I don't have that kind of money. I am using my savings just to survive and to try to restart the business.

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, I have photographs. I took many photos on my phone. I also have the insurance claim form that I submitted. I can send these to you if needed.
